elements.quote: Methods A systematic review of studies published between 2014 and 2024 was conducted across high-income and low- and middle-income countries.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: This study evaluated the impact of healthcare accreditation on quality outcomes across diverse hospital settings.
elements.reason: The abstract states the main objective of the review.

elements.quote: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract mentions inclusion criteria but does not specify what they were; no exclusion criteria are reported.

elements.quote: A systematic review of studies published between 2014 and 2024 was conducted
elements.reason: The abstract gives a date range but does not name information sources (databases) or when each was last searched.
The abstract does not mention any risk of bias assessment methods.

elements.quote: Findings were synthesised narratively following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) reporting guidance
elements.reason: The abstract specifies the synthesis method used.

elements.quote: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies (13) but not the number of participants or study characteristics.

elements.quote: Healthcare accreditation is associated with improvements in patient safety, organizational performance, and quality of care across diverse settings.
elements.reason: Main outcomes are reported qualitatively but without numbers of studies/participants per outcome.

elements.quote: could not be meaningfully pooled in a meta-analysis owing to outcome heterogeneity
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted, so no summary estimate is required in the abstract.

elements.quote: with stronger effects in high-income countries compared to low- and middle-income countries
elements.reason: The abstract compares groups and indicates the direction of effect and which group is favored.

elements.quote: The magnitude of effect varied substantially across studies and could not be meaningfully pooled in a meta-analysis owing to outcome heterogeneity.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity/inconsistency is noted, but the abstract does not broadly summarize limitations such as risk of bias or imprecision.

elements.quote: The findings suggest that while accreditation contributes to quality improvement, its sustainability depends on contextual factors including governance, work-force capacity and system-level support.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation and implications in the conclusion.
The abstract does not mention funding for the review.
The abstract does not report registration name or number (PROSPERO ID appears only in the methods section, not the abstract).

elements.quote: Healthcare accreditation evaluates hospitals against established standards to promote continuous quality improvement. However, its long-term effectiveness on healthcare quality and patient satisfaction remains debatable, highlighting the need for enhanced standards and stakeholder support.
elements.reason: The abstract background describes the current state of knowledge (accreditation evaluates hospitals against standards) and identifies the key uncertainty (long-term effectiveness remains debatable).

elements.quote: its long-term effectiveness on healthcare quality and patient satisfaction remains debatable, highlighting the need for enhanced standards and stakeholder support. This study evaluated the impact of healthcare accreditation on quality outcomes across diverse hospital settings.
elements.reason: The need for the review is explained by the ongoing debate over accreditation's long-term effectiveness, motivating this systematic review.
No prior systematic reviews on this topic are identified or cited, and no justification for an update or replication of existing reviews is provided in the retrieved evidence.
This is a review of experiences and challenges in sustaining quality accreditation (with narrative synthesis), not a review of intervention effects requiring a described mechanism of action.
The review does not evaluate a complex intervention with components requiring a logic model; it synthesises experiences and challenges of accreditation sustainability.

elements.quote: This study evaluated the impact of healthcare accreditation on quality outcomes across diverse hospital settings.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly states the review objective, addressing the impact of healthcare accreditation on quality outcomes across hospital settings.

elements.quote: P - Population: Hospitals (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, private, and specialty). I - Intervention: Accredited healthcare organization. C - Comparison: Not applicable. O - Outcomes: Quality, Patient safety, organizational performance. S - Study Design: Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies.
elements.reason: The review states its planned comparisons using an explicit PICOS framework, with comparison noted as not applicable.

elements.quote: P - Population: Hospitals (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, private, and specialty). I - Intervention: Accredited healthcare organization. C - Comparison: Not applicable. O - Outcomes: Quality, Patient safety, organizational performance. S - Study Design: Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies.
elements.reason: PICOS framework specifies population, intervention, outcomes, and eligible study designs; inclusion criteria also state hospital settings and involved stakeholders.

elements.quote: Peer-reviewed journals should be in English and published between 2014 and 2024.
elements.reason: Report characteristics specified: publication year range (2014-2024), English language, peer-reviewed status; non-English and no-full-text excluded.

elements.quote: Studies that reported the construct only qualitatively, used non-convertible categorical outcomes, or lacked dispersion statistics were excluded from pooling and analysed narratively.
elements.reason: The review distinguishes exclusion from pooling (outcome not convertible/reported) but does not explicitly distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus not reported; PRISMA flow shows 'not reporting relevant outcomes' as an exclusion reason only.

elements.quote: Three of the thirteen included studies reported quantitative ratings of accreditation's perceived impact on quality on a 5-point Likert scale
elements.reason: Grouping is described (three studies with comparable Likert data summarised descriptively; ten in narrative synthesis; subgroup analyses by income setting and accreditation body planned), but groups are not clearly linked to comparisons in the review objectives (comparison listed as 'Not applicable').
No rationales are provided for notable eligibility restrictions such as the 2014-2024 date limit or English-language restriction.
No date on which any database or source was last searched is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence; only a publication-year range (2014 to 2024) is given.

elements.quote: A comprehensive literature search was performed in the following databases: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Medline, and Science Direct, from 2014 to 2024
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but no search interface/platform or database coverage dates are specified; the 2014-2024 range refers to publication dates of articles, not database coverage. (Results also mention Web of Science and Cochrane Library, text_7, inconsistently with Methods.)
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories searched for studies are reported; PROSPERO is mentioned only as the protocol registration site, not as a searched source.
No websites or search engines searched to identify studies are reported.
No organisations or manufacturers contacted to identify studies are named.
No contact with individuals to identify studies is described.

elements.quote: Boolean operators, such as OR and AND, were used to conduct a manual search using the reference list to refine the search results.
elements.reason: Reference list searching is mentioned, but the types of reference lists examined (e.g., of included studies or relevant reviews) are not specified.
No backward or forward citation searching with seed reports, citation index/platform, or search date is reported.
No journals or conference proceedings browsed directly as sources are reported.

elements.quote: A comprehensive literature search was performed in the following databases: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Medline, and Science Direct, from 2014 to 2024... A literature search was conducted using a strategy that employed a combination of keywords and Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms. Boolean operators, such as OR and AND, were used... A detailed search strategy is attached in supplementary file 2.
elements.reason: Databases, date range, and a general approach (keywords/MeSH, Boolean operators) are described, and one example search string is given, but the full database-specific strategies are only in a supplementary file not shown; also the Results report searches in Web of Science and Cochrane Library, which are not listed in the Methods search description.

elements.quote: Peer-reviewed journals should be in English and published between 2014 and 2024... Non-English articles and manuscripts without fulltext articles were excluded.
elements.reason: Limits (date range 2014-2024, English language, peer-reviewed, full-text availability) are described, but they are not explicitly justified by reference to the eligibility criteria.
No published search approaches, filters, or hedges are cited, and no adaptations are described.
No evidence that natural-language processing or text-analysis tools were used to identify or refine search terms.
No evidence that translation tools were used to translate search strings between sources.
No validation of the search strategy is described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No peer review of the search strategy (e.g., PRESS) is reported.
The search appears concept-block based rather than PICO-based, but the final conceptual structure and its development are not described.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers screened the titles and abstracts against the eligibility criteria and resolved any disagreements through discussion. Subsequently, full-text articles were evaluated for methodological rigor, quality, and relevance.
elements.reason: Two reviewers are reported for both title/abstract screening and full-text assessment.

elements.quote: Two independent reviewers screened the titles and abstracts against the eligibility criteria
elements.reason: Independence of reviewers is explicitly stated for screening stages.

elements.quote: resolved any disagreements through discussion... Any remaining disagreements were resolved by a third reviewer.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution via discussion and a third reviewer is described for both screening stages.
No evidence of contacting study investigators for eligibility information; no indication this was needed.
No translation of abstracts or articles reported; non-English articles were excluded, so no translation methods apply.

elements.quote: 112 records flagged as ineligible by automation tools
elements.reason: Automation tools are mentioned as removing records before screening (also in the PRISMA flow diagram), but their integration into the selection process is not described in the methods.
No externally derived classifier is identified by version or reference; only a mention of records flagged by automation tools without describing any classifier.
No internally derived classifier is reported.
No machine-learning prioritisation or stopping rules are reported.
No crowdsourcing platforms are reported.
No previously screened datasets used to eliminate records are reported.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed by two independent reviewers using a standardized form.
elements.reason: Number of reviewers collecting data (two) is explicitly reported.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed by two independent reviewers using a standardized form.
elements.reason: Independence of the two data extractors is explicitly stated.

elements.quote: Discrepancies were resolved through consensus with a third reviewer.
elements.reason: Disagreement resolution process (consensus with third reviewer) is described.
No process for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators is reported.
No automation tools for data collection are described; automation tools are mentioned only for screening record removal, not data extraction.
Non-English articles were excluded, so translation for data collection does not apply.
No evidence of data extraction from figures; software for figure extraction not applicable.
No decision rules for selecting data from multiple reports or resolving inconsistencies among multiple reports are described.

elements.quote: O - Outcomes: Quality, Patient safety, organizational performance.
elements.reason: Outcome domains are listed in the PICOS framework, but no definitions of each outcome domain are provided.
No time frame of measurement is specified for any outcome domain in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not state whether all results compatible with each outcome domain (all measures, time points, analyses) were sought.

elements.quote: Outcome commensurability for the meta-analysis was defined a priori as: (i) measurement of the same construct... (ii) reporting of effect on continuous scale convertible to standardized mean difference (SMD); and (iii) availability of pre-and post-accreditation comparator data... Studies that reported the construct only qualitatively, used non-convertible categorical outcomes, or lacked dispersion statistics were excluded from pooling and analysed narratively.
elements.reason: A process for selecting which results to collect/analyse is described, but it addresses meta-analysis commensurability rather than a general rule for which compatible results within each outcome domain were collected.
No changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance are reported in the retrieved evidence, so there is nothing to report with rationale.
No changes to processes for selecting results within outcome domains are reported in the retrieved evidence.
The manuscript does not identify which outcomes were considered most important for interpreting conclusions or provide a rationale for prioritisation.

elements.quote: Data extraction was performed by two independent reviewers using a standardized form. ... P - Population: Hospitals (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, private, and specialty). I - Intervention: Accredited healthcare organization. C - Comparison: Not applicable. O - Outcomes: Quality, Patient safety, organizational performance. S - Study Design: Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method studies.
elements.reason: PICOS elements and outcome constructs (quality, patient safety, organizational performance) and contextual moderators (income setting, accreditation body, hospital type) are described, but a complete, explicit list and definition of all data items collected in the standardized extraction form is not provided.
No statement describing assumptions made about missing or unclear study information (e.g., handling of missing data during extraction) appears in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The narrative synthesis followed Synthesis Without Meta-Analyses (SWiM) reporting principles, (Campbell et al., BMJ 2020;368:l6890; the completed SWiM checklist is provided as Supplementary File 3)
elements.reason: The SWiM guidance is cited as the tool informing which data items (direction of effect, vote-counting, contextual moderators) to collect for synthesis.

elements.quote: The calculated effect sizes included standardized mean difference and odds ratio with their respective 95% CI.
elements.reason: Effect measures (SMD, OR) were prespecified for the planned meta-analysis, and Hedges' g with 95% CI was reported for the three quantitative studies (text_8), but the meta-analysis was not performed and effect measures for the narrative synthesis outcomes (direction of effect, vote-counting) are not specified per outcome.
No thresholds or ranges for interpreting effect sizes (or their rationale) are reported; the I² > 50% threshold concerns heterogeneity model choice, not effect size interpretation.
Although convertibility to SMD is mentioned as an inclusion criterion for pooling, no methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure are described.
The choice of effect measure (SMD, OR, Hedges' g) is not justified; only the random-effects model choice is justified due to anticipated heterogeneity.

elements.quote: Outcome commensurability for the meta-analysis was defined a priori as: (i) measurement of the same construct ... (ii) reporting of effect on continuous scale convertible to standardized mean difference (SMD); and (iii) availability of pre-and post-accreditation comparator data ... Studies that reported the construct only qualitatively, used non-convertible categorical outcomes, or lacked dispersion statistics were excluded from pooling and analysed narratively.
elements.reason: The methods explicitly describe the a priori criteria determining which studies were eligible for the (planned) meta-analysis versus the narrative synthesis, i.e., the processes used to decide eligibility for each synthesis.

elements.quote: Outcome commensurability for the meta-analysis was defined a priori as: (i) measurement of the same construct ... (ii) reporting of effect on continuous scale convertible to standardized mean difference (SMD); and (iii) availability of pre-and post-accreditation comparator data, or accredited vs. non-accredited group comparison, with sample sizes and dispersion statistics. Studies that reported the construct only qualitatively, used non-convertible categorical outcomes, or lacked dispersion statistics were excluded from pooling and analysed narratively.
elements.reason: The methods describe data preparation rules for synthesis, including convertibility of continuous outcomes to SMD and handling of studies lacking dispersion statistics (analysed narratively rather than pooled). However, explicit handling of missing summary statistics (e.g., imputation or contacting authors) and other data conversion details are not described, so reporting is partial.

elements.quote: A summary of hospital accreditation challenges across the included studies is presented in Table 1.
elements.reason: A summary table (Table 1) of study characteristics and challenges is referenced, but the Methods section does not describe the tabular structures or the data included in them; the table itself appears in the Discussion without a methods description.

elements.quote: The risk of bias across the included studies is illustrated in a heatmap (Fig. 2).
elements.reason: A heatmap for risk of bias and the PRISMA flow diagram (Fig. 1) are mentioned, but these relate to study selection and risk of bias rather than display of individual study results and syntheses; no graphical methods for displaying synthesis results (e.g., planned forest or funnel plot presentation of results) are described as used, since meta-analysis was not performed.
No basis for ordering or grouping studies within Table 1 or any figure is reported anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
A heatmap (Fig. 2) is a non-standard display, but no rationale for choosing it is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: All analyses were conducted in RevMan 5.4 (Cochrane, 2020).
elements.reason: Although RevMan 5.4 is mentioned in the retained pre-specified plan, no statistical synthesis/meta-analysis was actually performed, so reporting software for statistical synthesis does not apply.

elements.quote: The narrative synthesis followed Synthesis Without Meta-Analyses (SWiM) reporting principles, (Campbell et al., BMJ 2020;368:l6890; the completed SWiM checklist is provided as Supplementary File 3), summarising direction of effect, vote-counting based on direction, and key contextual moderators
elements.reason: The alternative synthesis method (SWiM narrative synthesis with vote-counting by direction) is described and justified due to outcome heterogeneity precluding pooling.

elements.quote: Findings were therefore synthesised narratively following the SWiM reporting guidance ... rather than meta-analytically pooled.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was performed; only a pre-specified (unexecuted) plan mentions a random-effects model.

elements.quote: The number of studies included in the meta-analysis was limited ... Findings were therefore synthesised narratively
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted, so no statistical method was used.

elements.quote: Heterogeneity between these studies was extreme (I² = 99.6%) ... we therefore did not pool them and report each study individually.
elements.reason: Although I² is reported descriptively, no meta-analysis was performed, so heterogeneity assessment methods for pooling do not apply.

elements.quote: A random-effects model (Der Simonian-Laird estimator) was used
elements.reason: This appears only in the retained pre-specified analysis plan that was explicitly not performed; no random-effects meta-analysis was conducted.

elements.quote: Findings were therefore synthesised narratively ... rather than meta-analytically pooled.
elements.reason: No random-effects meta-analysis was performed.

elements.quote: The following meta-analytic procedures were prespecified but not performed
elements.reason: No random-effects meta-analysis was conducted; sensitivity/subgroup plans were prespecified but not executed.

elements.quote: All analyses were conducted in RevMan 5.4 (Cochrane, 2020).
elements.reason: No Bayesian meta-analysis was performed or planned.

elements.quote: Findings were therefore synthesised narratively following the SWiM reporting guidance
elements.reason: No quantitative synthesis was performed, so no methods for statistical dependency were needed.

elements.quote: The following meta-analytic procedures were prespecified but not performed, as re-extraction revealed that included studies did not provide outcome data sufficiently homogeneous to permit defensible pooling
elements.reason: Planned meta-analyses are identified as not performed with explicit reasons (outcome heterogeneity precluding defensible pooling).

elements.quote: Cochran's Q test and I 2 statistics were used to assess heterogeneity; I 2 > 50% necessitated a random-effects model... Subgroup analyses by income setting (high-income vs. low-and middle-income) and accreditation body (JCI vs. national) were planned a priori.
elements.reason: Heterogeneity assessment methods (Q, I²) and subgroup analyses are described, but these were prespecified and not performed; actual exploration was narrative only, so specification is partial.

elements.quote: Subgroup analyses by income setting (high-income vs. low-and middle-income) and accreditation body (JCI vs. national) were planned a priori.
elements.reason: Subgroup factors and their levels are reported, but no expected direction of effect modification is stated, and these analyses were planned but not performed.

elements.quote: The following meta-analytic procedures were prespecified but not performed, as re-extraction revealed that included studies did not provide outcome data sufficiently homogeneous to permit defensible pooling
elements.reason: No subgroup analysis or meta-regression was conducted, so the study-level vs within-study contrast distinction does not apply.

elements.quote: The following meta-analytic procedures were prespecified but not performed
elements.reason: No subgroup analyses were performed, so methods for comparing subgroup effects do not apply.

elements.quote: The narrative synthesis followed Synthesis Without Meta-Analyses (SWiM) reporting principles... summarising direction of effect, vote-counting based on direction, and key contextual moderators (income setting, accreditation body, hospital type).
elements.reason: Informal exploration of heterogeneity via narrative synthesis is described with factors (income setting, accreditation body, hospital type), but levels are only partially specified and methods for exploring heterogeneity within the narrative synthesis are not fully detailed.

elements.quote: The following meta-analytic procedures were prespecified but not performed... For transparency, the pre-specified analysis plan is retained here.
elements.reason: No analyses of heterogeneity beyond the prespecified plan were reported, so there are no non-prespecified analyses to identify.

elements.quote: To assess robustness of the pooled estimate, leaveone-out sensitivity analyses were performed, removing each study in turn and re-estimating the pooled MD.
elements.reason: A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis is described in the methods, but the manuscript also states the pre-specified meta-analytic procedures were not performed because data could not be pooled, creating ambiguity about whether any sensitivity analysis was actually conducted; no results of sensitivity analyses are reported.

The manuscript does not identify whether the sensitivity analysis was pre-specified or not; it only notes that meta-analytic procedures and subgroup analyses were pre-specified, without clarifying the status of the leave-one-out sensitivity analysis.

elements.quote: Publication bias was evaluated visually using a funnel plot and statistically using Egger's regression test, with a p value < 0.10 indicating significant small-study effect.
elements.reason: Methods for publication bias (a form of reporting bias) are described, but no methods are reported for assessing risk of bias due to missing results in the synthesis; the meta-analysis was ultimately not performed.
No existing reporting-bias assessment tool was used; only funnel plot and Egger's test are mentioned, with no domains/items or overall judgement process reported.
No adaptations to an existing reporting-bias tool are described anywhere in the retrieved evidence.
No newly developed reporting-bias tool is described.

elements.quote: Quality assessment analysis, or what is also sometimes referred to as 'risk of bias, was assessed by two independent assessors according to the predetermined protocol criteria.
elements.reason: Two independent assessors performed risk of bias assessment; independence and consensus-based disagreement resolution (third reviewer) are described for related review steps, satisfying the reviewer-process requirement.
No processes for obtaining or confirming missing information from study investigators are reported, and none appear to have been used.
No automation tools were used for reporting-bias assessment; automation tools are mentioned only for screening eligibility.

No certainty/confidence assessment tool (e.g., GRADE) or version is reported. The manuscript only describes study-level quality/risk-of-bias categorization (good/fair/poor), not a certainty-of-evidence system.

elements.quote: questions related to confounding factors, characterizations, and outcome assessment risk of bias were prioritized, including selection biases... ascertainment bias... and causality assessment
elements.reason: Factors considered are described, but these pertain to study-level risk of bias/quality appraisal, not certainty in the body of evidence for outcomes; no formal certainty criteria are given.

elements.quote: The studies were categorized as good, fair, or poor. Good studies had a strong design with minimal bias, fair studies had some concerns, and poor studies had a high bias
elements.reason: Categories and their interpretation are defined, but these are study-level quality ratings, not rules for deriving an overall certainty level across a body of evidence for an outcome.
No review-specific certainty thresholds or rationales are reported; the review used narrative synthesis (SWiM) without a certainty assessment framework.
No adaptations to an existing certainty-assessment system are described; no certainty-assessment system is mentioned at all.

elements.quote: Quality assessment analysis, or what is also sometimes referred to as 'risk of bias, was assessed by two independent assessors according to the predetermined protocol criteria.
elements.reason: Two independent assessors are reported for quality/risk-of-bias assessment, but this is not a certainty assessment; no certainty-specific reviewer independence or disagreement-resolution procedures are described.
No processes for obtaining or confirming information from investigators in the context of certainty assessment are reported.
No automation tools for certainty assessment are used or reported, so this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: The risk of bias across the included studies is illustrated in a heatmap (Fig. 2).
elements.reason: Results presentation is described via a risk-of-bias heatmap, but no Summary of Findings table or method for reporting certainty-of-evidence results is described.
No standard phrases incorporating certainty, their interpretation, or source guidance (e.g., GRADE wording) are reported.

elements.quote: A total of 3684 records were identified through database searches (PubMed n = 912; Scopus n = 1,352; Embase n = 876; Web of Science n = 392; Cochrane Library n = 152). After removing 1,146 duplicates, 112 records flagged as ineligible by automation tools, and 66 records removed for other reasons, 2,360 records were screened against title and abstract; 2,122 were excluded at this stage.
elements.reason: Numbers identified, removed before screening, screened, and excluded at title/abstract screening are all reported in text and the PRISMA flow diagram (Fig. 1, figure_4).

elements.quote: Of the 238 reports sought for retrieval, 24 could not be retrieved, leaving 214 reports assessed for full-text eligibility. A further 202 reports were excluded (not focused on accreditation, n = 78; not reporting relevant outcomes, n = 62; wrong study design, n = 34; full text unavailable, n = 18; duplicate or overlapping data, n = 10).
elements.reason: Reports sought, not retrieved, assessed for eligibility, and excluded with itemized primary reasons are all reported.

elements.quote: Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis
elements.reason: Number of included studies (13) is reported; the flow diagram (figure_4) shows 'Studies included in narrative synthesis (n = 13)'. Reports at inclusion equal studies here (214 assessed, 202 excluded, 13 included), so included report numbers are effectively covered.

elements.quote: Studies included in narrative synthesis (n = 13)
elements.reason: No ongoing studies or associated reports are mentioned anywhere in the retrieved evidence, and the PRISMA flow diagram contains no ongoing-studies box, indicating this element does not apply.

elements.quote: A comprehensive literature search was performed in the following databases: PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Medline, and Science Direct, from 2014 to 2024
elements.reason: There is no indication this review is an update of a previous review; it is a new review registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024504564), so update reporting does not apply.

elements.quote: After removing 1,146 duplicates, 112 records flagged as ineligible by automation tools, and 66 records removed for other reasons
elements.reason: Records removed by automation tools (n = 112) are distinguished from other removals before screening, and the flow diagram (figure_4) shows 'Records marked as ineligible by automation tools (n = 112)' as a separate box.

elements.quote: A further 202 reports were excluded (not focused on accreditation, n = 78; not reporting relevant outcomes, n = 62; wrong study design, n = 34; full text unavailable, n = 18; duplicate or overlapping data, n = 10).
